props.title: The building blocks of ShowAI
props.lead: A content library holds projects. Projects contain folders and pages, and pages contain blocks and components. Templates and catalogs help you reuse them. Understanding these relationships makes the rest of the documentation easier to follow.

content.text: Click on any concept to view the definition; with "Open Document" you can jump to the detailed description.

nodes.label: Content Library
nodes.detail: A local directory that holds all projects, pages, components and templates. When the desktop app, local browser version, CLI and Agent point to the same content library, they see the same batch of content.

nodes.label: project
nodes.detail: Group related pages, folders, components and templates together. The project can record the host working directory, and the Agent's sessions in the same directory will share this project. Sync and assign permissions by project.

nodes.label: folder
nodes.detail: Hierarchical grouping within the project is only used to organize pages. Archiving a folder also hides its entire contents.

nodes.label: page
nodes.detail: Container with sequential layout, suitable for notes, reports and documents. New content defaults to pages.

nodes.label: whiteboard
nodes.detail: Containers that can be panned, zoomed, painted, and freely placed are suitable for organizing relationships and comparing plans. Pages and whiteboards can be nested within each other, and the same node will still be edited after expansion.

nodes.label: block
nodes.detail: Content in the container: text blocks such as paragraphs, titles, lists, and tables, as well as components such as charts, maps, and databases. Non-text blocks have a stable ID, which is used by agents and merges to locate them.

nodes.label: Component Catalog
nodes.detail: All pluggable components. Each component comes with descriptions, parameter rules and examples; when new expressions are needed, you can write React components and add them to the directory. The page saves an exact version of the component.

nodes.label: template
nodes.detail: Save content organization requirements and a base page, from which subtemplates can be combined. Expands into a separate page when applied; updating the template later will not change the generated page.

nodes.label: Export
nodes.detail: Package the page, along with the reader, data, and used components, into a single-file HTML, session fragment, or static website. The export is a snapshot, and subsequent modifications to the source page will not update the old file.

nodes.name: .showai
nodes.summary: The directory where all the content is located is in the user's home directory by default (`~/.showai `).
nodes.detail: It can be changed in "Settings → General → Content Library", and the CLI is specified with `--home `or environment variable `SHOWAI_HOME `.

content.text: What is the difference between a page and a whiteboard?
Both are containers and can hold the same content. The difference lies in the formatting method. The interfaces are called "pages" and "whiteboards" respectively.

props.note: The two types of containers can be nested recursively: for example, an analysis whiteboard is placed in a research report, and a detailed argumentation page is placed in the whiteboard.

content.text: The parent determines the outer frame, and the child container determines the internal layout.
. Expanding a nested container just changes to a larger workspace, and the same node is still edited; all levels share a resource file, a save mechanism, and an undo history. See details

It is the moving part of the page: a chart, a mind map, a database, a slider, or a React component you wrote yourself. Each component comes with descriptions, parameter rules, and examples, so the agent can pick the right component instead of writing a piece of HTML on the fly.

Save a page structure: what to write in each area, recommended components, and a basic page, and you can also combine sub-templates. Applying the template will expand a separate page, and updating the template later will not affect it.
Manage components and templates according to scope, and search in the following layers:
Versions created, imported or derived in the current project
A version that can be used by all projects on this machine
Explicitly register it globally and copy it together with dependencies
Obtain and verify the release package from the URL
Components and templates provided with the app
Update with the application; if you want to modify it, fork it into the project
, see if you develop it yourself
"Version" has two meanings in ShowAI, with different rules:

: Every time the page is saved, the revision (hash) you read will be checked. If someone else or the Agent changes it during this period, the save will be rejected and a conflict will be returned instead of being overwritten quietly.

Add content fingerprinting to determine an immutable piece of content. If you modify the content, you must save it as a new version; if you modify it in other projects, you must first derive it and record the source.

Save it locally. When saving fails or encounters a conflict, the draft will be retained and the status will show "Local draft has been retained"; you can "compare and merge" or "retain as copy". Fields that do not conflict with each other are automatically merged. See details

attrs.title: Why does the page lock the exact version of the component?

content.text: Recorded when the page references the component

. The same name and the same version may have different contents in different scopes. Simply comparing the name and version is not enough to confirm the identity. After locking, subsequent new versions of the component will not change the existing page, and the export can also bring the correct running code.

Export packages the page, along with the reader, data and used components, into a deliverable: single-file HTML, session fragment, or static website. The export is a snapshot, and the storage location is separate from the source page. Modifying the source page later will not update the exported file. See details
